A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPA research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original COMPAS and COCO experiments, simulated metric heatmaps, and attacker robustness results in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds ImSitu evaluations, ViT masking results, controlled shortcut experiments, and real-data attacker robustness results.

M1.justification: The direction-specific attackers and normalized predictability difference remain equivalent: v1 Equations 9–14 correspond to v2 Equations 1–6. Label-flipping quality equalization was already used in v1's COMPAS analysis. V2 expands its explanation and discloses experimental choices without establishing a changed DPA procedure.

E1.justification: ImSitu changes from a motivating example to an evaluated gender/activity dataset covering 205 activities in balanced and unbalanced subsets. Appendix F also introduces a COCO sink/not-sink task with controlled one-pixel shortcuts and tests with and without those shortcuts. Existing COMPAS and COCO masking coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V1's benchmark comparisons evaluate BA→ and Multi→ against DPA. V2 adds leakage amplification to the retained VGG COCO comparison (Table 9), and evaluates BAMALS alongside these metrics in the ViT COCO comparison (Table 2). These substantially expand the competing metric families tested. COMPAS comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: COCO adds ViT_b_16 alongside VGG16, and the reported unbalanced sampling constraint changes from 1/2–2 to 1/3–3; unchanged sample counts do not establish whether sampling was rerun. New protocols rank nine ImSitu models against concept sensitivity scores and evaluate shortcut-controlled COCO training and test conditions.

E4.justification: V2 adds attacker-width sensitivity experiments on ImSitu (Appendix D.2), a controlled hidden-bias intervention using shortcuts (Appendix F), and additional attribution case studies (Figure 5). The earlier synthetic robustness experiment and simulated heatmaps are retained in Appendices D.1 and J, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V1 displays uncertainty using unlabeled ± entries in its result tables. V2 explicitly identifies corresponding uncertainties as confidence intervals and links DPA uncertainty estimation to repeated label-flipping iterations. Neither version specifies iteration counts, seeds, or confidence levels, so an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: V2 adds ImSitu rankings, ViT masking scores, shortcut results, and real-data robustness findings. Retained VGG COCO DPA values also change: unbalanced/original increases from 0.0006 in v1 Table 4 to 0.0034 in v2 Table 9, alongside revised protocol reporting. COMPAS counts and scores remain unchanged in Tables 6–7.

T1.justification: The stated DPA range changes from (-1,1) in v1 Section 4.2 to [-1,1] in v2 Section 3.2. Appendix B recasts the conditional-probability directionality argument explicitly around DPA. The core metric definitions and the Multi→ absolute-difference derivation are retained.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly frames DPA as a single metric for classification and model selection, claiming it removes the need for multiple metrics to check directionality, sign, and balanced-data behavior. The underlying contribution claims about these capabilities, normalization, and attacker robustness are retained.

C2.justification: New Section 5.2 explains that aggregation can hide opposing effects for individual attribute–task pairs. The hiring example is revised to equal acceptance rates with unequal counts and adds an explicit warning about under-reporting amplification. V2 also develops model-selection applications and interpretations involving unlabeled background cues and shortcuts.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly documents the inverse-cross-entropy quality function and attacker optimizers, learning rates, epochs, batch sizes, and depths. Appendices D.2 and F add robustness-network and shortcut construction/training details. These substantially expand reproducibility information. V1's forthcoming-code statement disappears; neither PDF supplies a code link.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and central positioning against BA→, Multi→, and leakage amplification remain largely unchanged. V2 adds references on bias-amplification theory, language models, attacker sensitivity, shortcuts, concept sensitivity, model architectures, and the Rashomon effect to support its expanded experiments and applications.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method explanation. It folds the standalone leakage discussion into the motivation, combines experimental setup and results, moves COMPAS and several analyses into appendices, and introduces a dedicated limitations section. This substantially reorganizes the narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. V2 adds a directional-method diagram, model-ranking tables with colored discrepancies, a real-data robustness plot, and an attribution grid. COCO tables gain comparator rows, existing displays move to appendices, and uncertainty values are reformatted as subscripts.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially closes v1's validation gap by directly comparing against leakage amplification, checking model rankings against ImSitu concept sensitivity, and testing attacker robustness on real data. Explicit aggregation limitations and implementation details improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh new reporting errors: Appendix F claims only DPA increases although Multi→ also increases in Table 8, and Table 11's exact-ranking caption contradicts its entries.
